subject: Post-demo: runtime & token economics assumptions — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Peters <jpeters@acme-analytics.com>, ACME Platform Team <eng-sales@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: runtime & token economics assumptions — next steps

Hi Jordan / Platform team —

Thanks again for the demo time today — really helpful to see the pipeline use cases and how embeddings + short-form generation are going to be used across the product. Short summary of what we took away and the asks so we can get a scoped estimate over to you: 

Summary of workload assumptions (please confirm/correct):
- Typical request shape: embedding call (single small text, ~200 tokens) followed by a generation step for MR summary (average prompt 180 tokens + expected generation 380 tokens).
- Expected steady-state rps: 6–10 req/s during daytime business hours; peak bursts to 35–45 req/s for 2–5 minute windows tied to nightly pipeline runs and demo traffic.
- Concurrent active contexts: session-based KV cache reuse for ~60% of generation calls (helps; expecting continuous batching to aggregate prefixes).

Volume & unit-econ targets you mentioned on the call:
- Estimated monthly tokens (input+output): 30M – 45M per month (please confirm with your analytics team).
- Targeted run-rate budget: $15k–$25k / month. That suggests a target unit cost in the ~ $333–$833 per 1M tokens range (rough arithmetic).
- You asked if we can get to approximately $500 / 1M tokens at your committed run-rate — we can outline options.

Batching & runtime assumptions we used for the estimate:
- Continuous batching: we will assume an average effective batch size of 14 tokens per micro-batch during daytime traffic, with aggressive prefix caching for repeated session prompts.
- Concurrency profile: 6–10 sustained rps, with a 45 rps 5-minute burst profile for peak windows.
- Model choices: prefer quantized 8-bit variant of the Llama family for balance of latency and throughput; dedicated pool recommended at sustained 30M+ tokens for predictable unit economics.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm the monthly tokens window (30–45M) and whether bursts line up with your nightly pipeline at 02:00 UTC.
2) Confirm target budget / flexibility (is $15k a hard floor or can the team go to $30k committed for better unit pricing?).
3) If confirmed, we’ll send a formal pricing estimate (hosted vs dedicated) and a short appendix with concurrency/batching assumptions and expected latency percentiles.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (placeholder), demo-recording-20260821.mp4 (recording), acme-mrp-token-breakdown.xlsx (token calc sheet).

Thanks — I can get a draft estimate to you by tomorrow EOD once you confirm the volume range.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-demo: runtime & token economics assumptions — next steps

Thanks Monica — this is a great summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- Monthly tokens: narrow to 28M–36M for initial 3 months while we ramp. The 30–45M was an upper bound if the pilot goes well.
- Budget: we have $18k/mo approved for the pilot. If the price point requires a higher commit we can try to stretch to $24k/mo but need stronger proof of cost savings.
- Burst windows: yes, the nightly pipeline runs around 02:15 UTC and typically lasts 3–6 minutes; we may also have a once-a-week longer run tied to batch re-ingestion.

If you can show two pricing options (hosted with a predictable token rate + dedicated reserved pool at 1/3 term commitment), that would help. Also please call out where batching & prefix cache materially moves the unit price.

Jordan Peters
Director of Platform Engineering | Acme Analytics
jpeters@acme-analytics.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: runtime & token economics assumptions — (internal)

Rishi / Marissa — forwarding Acme's clarifying numbers. They are tighter: 28–36M tokens, $18k/mo pilot comfortable, potential to stretch to $24k/mo. Bursts at 02:15 UTC for ~3–6 minutes.

Suggested approach:
- Draft two scoped options:
  A) Hosted: pay-as-you-go with a volume discount tier at 25M+ tokens. Show $/1M baseline and a version assuming 10% effective improvement from continuous batching/prefix cache.
  B) Dedicated (3-month reserved): lower unit rate — target $500 / 1M or better if they commit to 30M+ monthly. Show expected latency p95 under their burst profile and how autoscaling handles 45 rps bursts.

Operational asks to include in the doc:
- Expected SLO (p95) for generation under burst (target < 600ms if possible).
- Plan for KV cache warm-up for nightly job; recommend small warm prefetch window to avoid cold penalties.

Can you draft the numbers? I will include the HubSpot link and ask for a PO option in the estimate.

Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T19:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: runtime & token economics assumptions — (internal)

Got it. Quick calc: if they land at 32M/mo and we hit effective batching + cache that reduces billed tokens by ~12% (fewer repeated prompts + prefix reuse), their effective billed tokens could be ~28.2M. At $500 / 1M that's about $14.1k/mo — fits under $18k pilot. If we price hosted baseline at $620 / 1M and offer a dedicated-savings path to $480 / 1M with a 3-month commit, that gives them clear upside and keeps margin.

Notes on assumptions to call out in the estimate:
- Billed tokens = raw tokens * (1 - cache_reuse_pct * reuse_effectiveness). I put reuse_effectiveness at 0.65 in the model.
- Burst sizing: assume autoscale can provide short-lived additional slots but p95 latency will depend on model variant; include a note on expected p99 degradation during sustained >90 rps (outside their profile).

I’ll put numbers in the spreadsheet and export. Marissa — can you draft the pricing table and add a short appendix showing latency curves for our suggested 8-bit variant?

Rishi

- A short ops runbook item explaining warm-up steps for the nightly job and an SLA paragraph for burst-handling.

If you can send the hosted estimate + the dedicated alternative by EOD PT I’ll loop in procurement and security (they will want the SOC2 docs).

Jordan
